query: If teams adopted the goal-management practices described by top performers, how much would achievement improve?

per_column.name: primary_lever
per_column.rationale: The choice of primary lever (market expansion, automation, process optimization, etc.) is a decision an actor can set/change, and aligns with 'goal-management practices' the query proposes adopting. It is intervenable.

per_column.name: action_plan_detail
per_column.rationale: Whether a goal has a single action vs. multi-step detailed plan is a settable practice — a direct instance of 'goal-management practices described by top performers.'

per_column.name: feedback_loop_present
per_column.rationale: Presence of a feedback loop is an intervenable practice teams could adopt; a lever the query explicitly frames as adoptable.

per_column.name: goal_specificity
per_column.rationale: Whether goals include baseline+target vs. target only is a configurable goal-setting practice — intervenable and consistent with the treatment set.

per_column.name: target_ambition_level
per_column.rationale: Ambition level of the target is a common cause: it influences both which practices/levers get adopted and the achievable percent_complete (more ambitious targets are harder to complete). Not named in query. Plausible confounder to adjust for.

per_column.name: time_horizon
per_column.rationale: Time horizon plausibly affects both which management practices are chosen and the likelihood/degree of completion. A genuine common cause not named in the query.

per_column.name: measurement_mechanism
per_column.rationale: The way progress is measured (financial metric, survey, KPI, turnover) is more a measurement/operationalization artifact than a common cause of both treatment and outcome; closer to how percent_complete is defined than a confounder.

per_column.name: goal_category_alignment
per_column.rationale: Goal category (revenue growth, satisfaction, cost reduction) is a domain that shapes both which levers/practices are applicable and baseline completion rates. A plausible common cause not named in the query.

judge.rationale: The added columns strongly realise the what-if claim. Multiple treatments (primary_lever, action_plan_detail, feedback_loop_present, goal_specificity) are genuine intervenable practices an actor could set/change and directly instantiate the 'goal-management practices' the query proposes adopting — satisfying requirement (a). For (b), several columns function as bona fide confounders that are common causes of both practice adoption and completion and were NOT named in the query: target_ambition_level, time_horizon, and goal_category_alignment. These demonstrate the capability under test. measurement_mechanism is better treated as a measurement/operationalization artifact of the outcome rather than a confounder. Overall this is a strong pass on the interventional what-if criterion.
